Engineering, Electrical and Computer Engineering Track, Ph.D.
Doctor of Philosophy in Engineering
The doctoral program leading to a Ph.D. degree in Engineering is housed in the Donaghey College of Science, Technology, Engineering, and Mathematics. Faculty, curriculum, and resources for this program are contributed by the School of Engineering and Engineering Technology, with support from the departments of Computer and Information Sciences, Construction Management, and Civil and Construction Engineering. The program is designed to provide a collaborative, interdisciplinary framework of graduate studies and research in engineering. Students enrolled in the Ph.D. program in Engineering select one of the two tracks:
1. Engineering, Electrical and Computer Engineering Track, Ph.D.
The Electrical and Computer Engineering track focuses on disciplines of electrical engineering and computer engineering, including embedded systems, robotics, analog and digital
electronics, control systems, cyber-physical systems, power grid, and communication systems.
2. Engineering, Mechanical Engineering Track, Ph.D.
The Mechanical Engineering track focuses on advanced solid and fluid mechanics, MEMS and microsystems, vibration analysis, applied numerical and finite element
methods, and smart materials.
Admission Requirements
In addition to the UA Little Rock Graduate School admission requirements, the applicants for the Ph.D. program in Engineering must also meet the following criteria:
Education:
Applicants must have at least one degree (bachelor’s or master’s) in engineering.
Applicants with only a bachelor’s degree in engineering must have an overall undergraduate GPA of 3.5 or better. Applicants with a master’s degree in engineering should have a master’s GPA of 3.5 or better.
Standardized test scores:
Applicants are required to submit GRE scores with the admission application. A combined total of 315 on the verbal and quantitative reasoning sections and a score of 3.5 on the analytical writing section will be expected.
The GRE may be waived for applicants who graduate from UA Little Rock with a master’s degree in electrical and computer engineering (thesis option) and a 3.5 GPA or higher. GRE requirements can be waived in exceptional cases or when the GRE is not offered in the applicant’s country.
English language requirement:
International students must satisfy the Graduate School TOEFL or IELTS test requirements.
Statement of purpose:
Applicants are required to submit a personal statement that should include their background, qualifications, and motivation for doctoral studies. The statement should also emphasize the applicant’s educational and research interests.
Letters of recommendation:
Applicants should arrange for three (3) letters of recommendation to be submitted to UA Little Rock on their behalf by individuals familiar with their academic background and educational interests.
Applicants are encouraged to contact engineering faculty for their research supervision. The availability and willingness of advisors will be considered in making admission decisions.
Application Deadlines:
March 31st for fall admission.
September 30th for spring admissions.
Summer admissions are not offered.
Conditional Admission
Applicants who do not meet all the admission requirements may be recommended for conditional admission by respective program coordinators. Conditionally admitted students must fulfill the requirements specified by the UA Little Rock Graduate School and the program Governance Committee. The requirements will be explained in the admission letter.
Graduate Assistantships
A limited number of graduate assistantships that support teaching and research opportunities are available to qualified full-time students with regular admissions. Tuition is paid for nine credits per semester, and a stipend is provided for living expenses. Students must pay registration fees, buy textbooks, and purchase any necessary support materials. For more information about graduate assistantships, the online application process, and other financial assistance opportunities, visit the Engineering Science and Systems doctoral program website. A student supported by a graduate assistantship must be a registered full-time student taking at least nine credit hours during the fall and spring semesters.
Transfer of Credit
The student can request up to 15 credit hours of graduate-level courses to be transferred. Only courses within five years of their completion can be accepted for transfer. Only courses with a grade of B or above are qualified to be transferred. All transferred courses should get the approval of the student’s advisor, the instructors of comparable UA Little Rock courses, and the track coordinator.
Program Requirements
In addition to the Graduate School requirements,
A. A student entering the Ph.D. program with a Bachelor’s degree will be required to complete a minimum of 30 hours of graded coursework at the 50000 level or above, including 18 hours at the 70000 level.
B. A student entering the Ph.D. program with a Master’s degree will be required to complete a minimum of 15 hours of graded coursework at the 70000 level
C. All doctoral students will be required to complete at least 32 doctoral research credit hours
D. In addition, students enrolled in the Ph.D. program must:
Take courses recommended by the supervisor
Maintain acceptable academic performance
Pass candidacy examinations
Pass proposal defense
Publish and present at least one paper at a peer-reviewed national/international conference
Have at least one paper accepted for publication in an internationally reputed journal with the student as the first author
Pass dissertation defense.
Engineering Curriculum
The student’s plan of study must be developed in conjunction with his/her Doctoral Dissertation Committee and filed with the appropriate track coordinator and the Engineering graduate coordinator.
Program Core
Engineering Seminar component – One credit hour
ECEG 71001 - Research Methodology
Or
ASCI 71801 - (was 7118) Research Ethics in Science and Eng.
Engineering mathematical foundations component – Six credit hours
As advised by the student’s research advisor or track coordinator.
Track Core Courses - 12 credit hours.
Required of students entering a Ph.D. program with a Bachelor’s degree.
Program Electives: 12 credit hours
A list of the core courses for each of the two program tracks, as well as examples of elective courses, is listed below. Students must choose three of the four listed core courses under their chosen track and four elective courses, usually from those listed under that track. Student may, with their advisors’ permission, choose elective courses from other tracks as necessary to further their research.
Dissertation Research:
29 credit hours for students entering the program with a Bachelor’s degree, and 41 credits for students entering the program with a Master’s degree.
Total Hours Required for the Program
72 hours for students entering the PhD program with a Bachelor’s degree and 48 hours for students entering the Ph.D. program with a Master’s degree.
Candidacy Exams
The program is designed so that the student is exposed to a breadth of knowledge through the program core and a depth of knowledge through the track core. Before beginning dissertation research formally, students are required to pass the candidacy exam. The candidacy exams can be waived if a student is awarded a Master’s degree with thesis option in Engineering at UA Little Rock with a GPA of 3.5 or above and continues the Ph.D. program in Engineering Science and Systems with the same advisor.
The candidacy exam will have a written and an oral component. The written component will test the student regarding fundamental knowledge at the advanced undergraduate level. The oral component will test the student’s ability to conduct research in their area of interest. A candidacy exam committee will be formed, including three faculty members who will prepare the problems for the written exam.
The candidacy exam structure is as follows:
The student can take the candidacy exam as soon as possible. The student can take the exam no later than the 3rd semester in the program. Students who do not take the exams by the 3rd semester will be treated as having failed in their first attempt.
The student must officially declare their intention to take the candidacy exam at the beginning of the semester in which they will first attempt it.
The student needs to attempt both components in the same semester, and must pass each separately. If the student fails to pass one or more components in the first attempt, they will have to retake those components in the next semester. Failure to pass the exam in two attempts will result in dismissal from the program, pending review by the Engineering Science and Systems Governance Committee. This review will be completed, and a decision will be conveyed to the student within the academic year in which they have taken the exam.
The students may contact the faculty members who prepare the problems for the written exam for necessary information such as syllabi and problem styles.
Decisions of the Track Candidacy Exam Committee will be supported by all the committee members present and will be any one of the following:
Pass
Pass with remedial coursework
Fail
In this case, the student will retake the oral component in the following semester on the same research topic; the student must submit a new report before retaking the oral exam.
Written Component
The written exam for each track will be 1 3-hour exam.
Each written exam should include three different subject areas. The problems should be prepared by three different faculty members, including the student’s advisor. The subject areas should be proposed by the advisor and approved by the track coordinator. The instructors may provide the syllabi and examples of problems for the selected topics.
Passing the exam requires an overall grade of 70% or above with at least 60% in each subject area.
Oral Component:
The oral exam for each track will be 1 1-hour exam.
The student will be given a research topic on which to submit a written report. The student must submit their report within one calendar month after the written exam.
Based on the report, the student will be questioned by the Track Candidacy Exam Committee.
Oral exams are scheduled no earlier than two weeks after the student’s report submission.
The advisor, in coordination with the track coordinator, will organize the oral exam.
Proposal Defense
A candidate must present their research proposal to their Doctoral Dissertation Committee within two semesters after passing the candidacy exam or the first 9 hours taken for the Doctoral Research Dissertation, whichever comes first. After the proposal defense, the Doctoral Dissertation Committee will vote to pass or fail the student. A student who fails the proposal defense must repeat the defense within a semester of their first attempt. If the student fails the proposal defense for a second time, they will be dismissed from the program, pending review by the Engineering Science and Systems Governance Committee.
Dissertation Defense
**Before the dissertation defense, students must submit the written dissertation and published papers to the Doctoral Dissertation Committee.
To complete the requirements for the doctoral degree, students will prepare and successfully defend a written dissertation in accordance with the Graduate School’s format and procedures. Students must orally defend their completed doctoral research to their Doctoral Dissertation Committee. After the dissertation defense, the Doctoral Dissertation Committee will vote to either pass or fail the student. A majority vote is required to pass. If a student fails the exam, they may be dismissed from the program, pending review by the Engineering Science and Systems Governance Committee.
Doctoral Dissertation Advisor
A doctoral student must receive approval from and declare an advisor no later than the second semester they are in the program. The advisor must be a faculty member of the School of Engineering and Engineering Technology
.
Doctoral Dissertation Committee
The Doctoral Dissertation Committee:
Can be constituted once the student has declared their dissertation advisor and must be completed by the end of their second semester in the program.
Must include a minimum of five (5) members and can include up to seven (7) members.
At least four (4) members should be School of Engineering and Engineering Technology
program faculty.
Can have one or more external members who are not Engineering Science and Engineering Technology program faculty.
Any exceptions(s) will be subject to the approval of the track coordinator and the graduate coordinator. If the dissertation advisor and the doctoral student are affiliated with different tracks, it is required that at least one faculty member on the committee belong to the student’s track.
Residency Requirement
After entering the School of Engineering and Engineering Technology Doctoral Program, the student must complete 18 hours on campus within four (4) consecutive semesters, with optional summer semesters. Of these 18 hours, at least six (6) must be research credits.
Courses in the Engineering Science and Systems Doctoral Program
The catalog description of the program core, track core, and elective courses, and the dissertation research courses that are part of the Engineering and Engineering Technology Doctoral Program, is also provided on the Computer and Information Sciences Department page in this catalog. Other courses may be approved in consultation between the student and their Doctoral Dissertation Committee.
Up to fifteen credit hours may be granted to the student for completing equivalent graduate coursework at other institutions. Such credit must be exclusive of thesis or other exit project credits, be no more than 5 years old at the time of transfer, and must have a letter grade of B or better. In some cases, students may be required to balance their transfer credit with a corresponding increase in research hours.
Students interested in requesting a credit transfer should discuss the request with their doctoral dissertation advisor and appropriate track coordinator. The request must also be approved by the Engineering and Engineering Technology graduate coordinator and the dean of the Graduate School before the transfer of credit can be granted.2
For a student with an M.S. earned from UA Little Rock, all lecture credit hours earned in the M.S. program with a grade of B or above count towards the Ph.D. program.
